summary: We are testing whether two combined optimizations — precomputing coprime/Dedekind-sum lists and replacing mpmath's pure-Python arithmetic with gmpy2 MPFR for low-precision iterations — can reduce npartitions(10^6) runtime from ~23ms (iter-1 baseline) to ~14ms while preserving exact correctness. An ablation arm isolates the contribution of each optimization.
key_points: Main arm (h-main) applies both optimizations: (1) precompute per-j coprime (h, D) pair lists to eliminate ~14,641 gcd calls and ~9,028 lru_cache dispatches per invocation (predicted saving ~5ms), and (2) use gmpy2 C-level cosh/sinh/sqrt/div for 239 of 243 iterations where prec ≤ 1000 bits (predicted saving ~3ms). Combined predicted runtime: ~14ms.

Ablation arm (h-ablation) applies only the coprime precomputation, keeping the original mpmath _d function. Predicted runtime: ~18ms. If the ablation matches h-main (~14ms), the gmpy2 _d optimization contributes nothing and should be dropped.

Confirmation criteria: (1) correctness — sympy/ntheory/tests/test_partitions.py must pass for both arms; (2) h-main mean runtime ≤ 16ms (vs baseline ~23ms); (3) h-ablation mean runtime between 17–20ms, demonstrating that gmpy2 _d adds measurable benefit (~4ms) beyond coprime precomputation alone.

Key risk: gmpy2 context-switching overhead or precision mismatches could negate the _d speedup or cause correctness failures. Diagnostic: if correctness fails, increase guard bits from 50 to 100; if no speedup, profile to check whether overhead shifted to gmpy2 context management.

Unlocked parameters (M_factor=0.24, precision_margin=1.1x+100, dynamic_precision_offset=50, gmpy2_prec_cutoff=1000, guard_bits=50) are all justified by probing data and unchanged from validated defaults where applicable.
